summary_of_changes: Created password_generator.py implementing the architecture exactly: public constants MIN_LENGTH=8, MAX_LENGTH=1024, and generate_password(length=12) -> str. Character pools (_UPPER, _LOWER, _DIGITS, _SPECIAL, _ALL) are built from the standard-library string module (ascii_uppercase, ascii_lowercase, digits, punctuation) and frozen at import. _validate_length() rejects bool explicitly via an isinstance(length, bool) check before the general int check (raising TypeError), rejects any other non-int with TypeError, and rejects in-range-typed but out-of-bounds ints with ValueError. generate_password() draws one guarantee character per required class via secrets.choice, fills the remaining length-4 positions from the combined _ALL pool via secrets.choice, then shuffles the full buffer in place with a hand-rolled Fisher-Yates (_secure_shuffle) using secrets.randbelow(i+1) as the swap index, and returns ''.join(chars). No import of the random module anywhere. The module is pure (no I/O, no logging, no global mutable state beyond frozen constants) and does not import password_strength.py. Module and function docstrings mirror password_strength.py's style (module docstring stating public API and purity guarantees, function docstring with Args/Returns/Raises). No test files were created or modified.
